description: Rade Djukanovic describes using IESVE on public and private buildings in Serbia, including schools, kindergartens, hospitals and offices. Thermal models were compared with utility bills and calibrated using measured temperatures, humidity and carbon-dioxide concentrations. MacroFlo airflow analysis and hourly ApacheSim thermal simulation assessed natural and mechanical ventilation strategies, while other analyses considered heat pumps, insulation and shading. The underlying measurement period is limited and the buildings are unnamed. Ventilation scenarios are not evidence of independently established disease-prevention effects. This public HTML case narrative is published by IES and can be read without payment. Its reuse licence is not stated. Access to the described software, input data and project models is not established by the public page. The source does not give a complete study period or all spatial and temporal model resolutions. Reported results are provider claims and have not been independently reproduced. The case supports the documented infrastructure simulation use and is linked to the named modelling resources. Only metadata and the case description were inspected; no data or model files were downloaded.
